hiddenCases.name: table is three rows of two

exercise2.hint: One loop hands you a row, which is itself a list. Printing that row gives you the brackets too, so a second loop is what gets you down to the numbers.

questions.explain: The first index picks the row and the second picks the item inside it, so grid[1][0] is the first item of the second row.

questions.prompt: What does len(grid) report for grid = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]?
questions.explain: len() counts the items of the outer list, which are the rows. The width of a row is len(grid[0]).

questions.prompt: Put these lines in order so every number in the table is printed on its own line.
questions.explain: Each loop is indented inside the one above it, and the print sits deepest of all, so it runs once per element rather than once per row.

questions.prompt: A single loop, for row in table, prints what on each pass?
choices: A whole row, brackets and all
questions.explain: Each item of the outer list is a list, so printing it shows the brackets. That is the tell that you need the inner loop.
